svg.text: Agent E2, Knowledge: what "Private Cloud Operations Management with VMware Cloud Foundation" knowledge is made of
288 files, about 327K tokens. Two bodies of knowledge, one layered product, three ways to find a fact, one anatomy for every file. Read top to bottom.
Two bodies of knowledge, in every answer
The method says how to operate VCF. The product says what VCF is and does. Shared vocabulary and exact values serve both.
How to operate VCF, in VCF terms and examples.
the framework across pillars: health check,
how to read telemetry: input types, interval,
KPI design, KPI vs SLA, noisy neighbour
What each component is and does, down to the counter.
The product VCF Operations: its role, alert definitions,
report suite, dashboards and features as built.
Windows and Linux: a separate layer, not Broadcom
products, not part of the VM. cpu, memory, storage, system.
The agent's vocabulary: one English word per
concept, other names users say, confusable
pairs (Usage vs Utilization, KPI vs SLA).
Exact values, loaded into SQLite, not chunked:
A number must not depend on retrieval luck.
The product is a stack: a metric lives in the layer that produces it
Not in the object that stores it. A VM is a virtual motherboard; the Guest OS above it is a separate layer. Tag: layer.
Windows or Linux inside the VM
Not a Broadcom product, not part of the VM.
The VM as the hypervisor presents it
Example: vCPU Ready, the consumer view.
The provider view of the same resource.
Tag only: no folder of its own.

Consumer and provider show up as two vantage points on one resource: a consumer VM seen from the virtual motherboard, the provider ESXi seen from the hypervisor. Same word, different layer, different meaning.
Why it matters: "ESXi CPU Ready is high, so the host waits for CPU" is a wrong reading, because Ready is a consumer metric. The layer tag keeps the two apart in search.
One fact, three ways to find it
The folder tree holds one slice. Tags and links hold the others. Retrieval filters on any tag; the model follows any link.
One metric, one object type, one file. Kind: metric-meaning. Class: contention.
Listed in vm-health-check, part of the
the cluster KPI in the SP5 Framework.
Tags: scope, technology, pillar, product, object, layer, instance, metric_class. Links: internal_derive, same_name, same_meaning, related. Together they are the expert's map of what is read together.
One file: the same anatomy for every fact
One fact per bullet, so a mistake stays on one line. Templates keep section names the same, so a question finds the same kind of section everywhere.
